function · `import { readPackageManifest } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

#### `packageProblems`

function · `import { packageProblems } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

What is wrong with a package for the contract it ships: the contract's name must be the manifest's, the manifest
must speak this SDK's link protocol (its format is checked by the schema), and a system that runs one instance
(`instances: 'one'`) runs only as `main`. Empty when they agree.

```ts
function packageProblems(contract: AnyContract, manifest: SystemPackageManifest, instance?: InstanceName): string[];
```

Refers to: [`InstanceName`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.primitives-ts#core-instancename), [`SystemPackageManifest`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.package-ts#core-systempackagemanifest).

#### `PackageManifestError`

class · `import { PackageManifestError } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

A `system.json` that could not be read or does not fit `SystemPackageManifest`.

```ts
class PackageManifestError extends Error {
  readonly name: "PackageManifestError";
  /** The file it is about. */
  readonly file: string;
  constructor(file: string, message: string, options?: { cause: unknown });
}
```

#### `builtPackageManifest`

function · `import { builtPackageManifest } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

The built copy of a manifest (`dist/system.json`): the source's facts with the built entries. Any file hashes are
dropped; `pack` writes them for the files it packs.

```ts
function builtPackageManifest(manifest: SystemPackageManifest, entries: BuiltEntries): SystemPackageManifest;
```

Refers to: [`SystemPackageManifest`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.package-ts#core-systempackagemanifest).

#### `packedPackageManifest`

function · `import { packedPackageManifest } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

A manifest that lists the sha-256 of every file packed beside it (paths relative to the package, forward slashes).

```ts
function packedPackageManifest(manifest: SystemPackageManifest, files: ReadonlyMap<string, Uint8Array>): SystemPackageManifest;
```

Refers to: [`SystemPackageManifest`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.package-ts#core-systempackagemanifest).

#### `packageFileProblems`

function · `import { packageFileProblems } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

What is wrong with a package's files against its manifest's hashes: a listed file missing or changed, or a file
the manifest doesn't list (`system.json` itself aside). Empty when they match; a manifest without hashes matches
nothing (it was never packed).

```ts
function packageFileProblems(manifest: SystemPackageManifest, files: ReadonlyMap<string, Uint8Array>): string[];
```

Refers to: [`SystemPackageManifest`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.package-ts#core-systempackagemanifest).

#### `packageManifestText`

function · `import { packageManifestText } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

The manifest as `system.json` text: two-space JSON with a final newline, so a written file diffs cleanly.

```ts
function packageManifestText(manifest: SystemPackageManifest): string;
```

Refers to: [`SystemPackageManifest`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.package-ts#core-systempackagemanifest).

#### `BuiltEntries`

interface · `import { BuiltEntries } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

The entries a build wrote, relative to the built folder: `server/main.js` and, with renderers, `client/index.js`.

```ts
interface BuiltEntries {
  readonly server: string;
  readonly client?: string;
}
```
